jobDescription: Two regional distribution centres receive inbound stock from suppliers and replenish stores across the north of the region. The Warehouse Operations Planner schedules labour and dock doors, monitors inbound and outbound service levels, leads structured improvement reviews on receiving and keeps the receiving standard work current. Improvement results are reported against a documented baseline, and the role requires a recognised process-improvement certification. The planner works closely with the shift leads, the site quality coordinator and the transport desk, and hands weekly exceptions to the site managers every Monday.
requirements: Plans weekly labour rosters and dock-door schedules for the two distribution centres.
Monitors inbound and outbound service levels and reports exceptions to the site managers.
Leads structured process-improvement reviews on receiving using a recognised method.
Demonstrates a measured reduction in dock-to-stock time against a documented baseline.
Holds a recognised process-improvement certification and keeps receiving standard work current.

evidence.text: Planned weekly labour rosters and dock-door schedules for two distribution centres, balancing inbound appointments against shift capacity in the yard management tool.
Reported daily inbound and outbound service levels to the site managers and raised exception notes when carrier arrivals missed their appointment window by more than an hour.
Ran structured improvement reviews (define, measure, analyse, improve, control) on receiving-dock delays with the shift leads and the site quality coordinator.
Reduced average dock-to-stock time from 9.2 hours to 7.4 hours between January and June 2024, measured from the yard management tool's receipt timestamps.
Maintained the receiving standard work documents for both sites and trained new receiving operatives on them during their first week of onboarding, using the documents as the training checklist.

Work sample: the dock-to-stock review pack, with the January baseline extract (mean 9.2 hours), the June extract (mean 7.4 hours), a method note defining the receipt and put-away timestamps, and the site manager's sign-off page.
HR verification note: the candidate's Lean Six Sigma Green Belt certificate (number GB-48213) was checked against the issuing body's public register and is listed as valid until 2027.
Recruiter logistics note: candidate prefers a Monday start and has asked whether the role includes the weekend peak rota.
